chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim al-Karkhi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If a believer were to invite me to the food of an arm of a sheep, I would accept, and that would be from the religion; and if a polytheist or a hypocrite were to invite me to the food of a whole camel, I would not accept, and that would be from the religion. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, refused me the scum of the polytheists and the hypocrites and their food.'

key_terms.ذِرَاعِ: arm (of a sheep, indicating a modest portion)
key_terms.زَبْدَ: scum or best part (of the polytheists)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet decline a large meal from a polytheist but accept a small one from a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of 'selective hospitality,' where the spiritual purity of the host outweighs the material value of the meal, reflecting the Prophet's preference for intimate communion with believers over grandeur with the unworthy. The rejection of the 'scum' (zabd) of polytheists underscores the theological principle that their status renders their offerings less spiritually beneficial, a view supported by Shia exegetes who link this to the preservation of communal identity and faith. This practice serves as a practical application of maintaining religious boundaries while fostering strong social bonds within the community of believers.
